chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: The Rendezvous floor show, Joe E. Lewis, and the Polar Bear Garden
summary: The band handles a tough floor show with sixteen girls and stars like Joe E. Lewis; he takes the hot choruses and fakes parts he cannot read.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yes, we did. But, I didn't know that then. And, so, we went in there and they had - of course, a very tough floor show - very tough floor show --- thank God for Joe Hooven-- you know. Of course, all the guys in the band could read very good but me.
All right but thank God for Joe Hooven but still - I mean he had to play the lead trumpet player but that really wasn't your job - was it? I mean---
Editor's note: Some of the above passages were hampered by a defective recording tape.
No - no. I played all the second. I could fake second parts as good as I can read them---
But, also, your main job was to take hot breaks and things - wasn't it.

Well, I took all the choruses --- you know, if there were dancing girls going - it would be between the clarinet and me to divide up choruses while they danced and, in all the bandnumbers, if there was a hot place for the cornet, that was me.
And, all that. And, then, I was good at harmony -- you remember the time I told you - I found out I could sing harmony --

Well, that goes on the horn as well - and I could --- even if the arrangement was too tough for me to read, I would fake a part just as good--- you know, it sounded just as good. But, we had a tough floor show there because we had a line of, I think, 16 girls -- God, that's as many as you have in a big stage in a big theater--- and, of course, we had Joe E. Lewis -- first time I'd ever heard him ---that's when he was a young man and we had Babe Kane - the ingénue.
And, he married the boss--- Johnny Fogarty--- and moved to California; I don't know whether they're still alive--- but, anyway, and then we had the
William Sisters -- and Demsey--used to come in -- I think he married one of the William Sisters---
Yeah--- Demsey used to come in and that's the kind of people who hung around in there. And, it was just--- oh, I liked that very much. It was just a hell of a place to play.
It was a fancy place - wasn't it?

Oh, very, very, very. And, they had a garden outside for summer; they called it the "Polar Bear Garden" and it was kind of clever; they painted blocks of ice and snow and polar bears all around the fence -- it went all around the garden. It made you feel cool whether you were cool or not--- you know. And, uh, of course, you know, Chicago is a very hot place in the summer.
